candidate.answerReason: Squaring yields candidates x=26 and x=−9. Their original left-hand sides are 5 and −5 respectively, so only 26 is a true root and −9 is extraneous.

methods.label: Clear the denominator and square
methods.explanation:
The square root must be real and the denominator must be nonzero, so \(x>-10\). On this domain, multiplying by \(\sqrt{x+10}\) is valid and gives
\[
x+10-6=5\sqrt{x+10},
\]
so
\[
x+4=5\sqrt{x+10}.
\]
Squaring removes the radical, but it may introduce a candidate whose two sides had opposite signs before squaring. We obtain
\[
(x+4)^2=25(x+10),
\]
which simplifies to
\[
x^2-17x-234=(x-26)(x+9)=0.
\]
Every original solution must therefore be \(26\) or \(-9\). Checking both in the original equation gives
\[
x=26:\quad 6-\frac66=5,
\]
\[
x=-9:\quad 1-\frac61=-5\ne5.
\]
Thus \(26\) is the only true root, while \(-9\) is extraneous. Since \(-10<-9<-6\), the answer is choice B.
